node-1.label: Patient presented with dyspnea and syncope during exercise

node-2.label: Patient is in their 80s; medical history includes essential hypertension and Parkinson disease

node-3.label: For the past year, patient reported dyspnea on exertion and exercise intolerance, with difficulty walking more than 100m

node-4.label: Patient experienced syncope during a bicycle ride, with loss of consciousness for a few minutes followed by complete recovery

node-5.label: Physical examination: blood pressure 150/78 mm Hg; chest auscultation revealed normal breath and heart sounds without murmurs

why.why: ECG/Holter now documents high-grade AV block (first-degree AV block with bifascicular block, intermittent third-degree AV block, minimum HR 36 bpm), which directly explains exertional dyspnea and syncope. Echocardiography shows normal EF and wall motion, so no severe structural abnormality refutes bradyarrhythmia; left atrial enlargement and mild pulmonary hypertension are secondary changes. Expert analyses both support cardiac syncope as the leading diagnosis, so confidence is raised from 0.8 to 0.95.

The confirmed high-grade AV block provides a clear cardiac mechanism for exertional syncope, while normal blood pressure, normal examination, and exertional (not orthostatic) loss of consciousness argue against autonomic dysfunction. Expert analyses also regard autonomic dysfunction as less likely, so confidence is reduced from 0.25 to 0.1.

Exertional dyspnea is explained by the confirmed high-grade AV block and secondary mild pulmonary hypertension; normal chest auscultation, absence of pulmonary findings, and the documented bradyarrhythmia make pulmonary disease unlikely. Expert analyses support this, so confidence is reduced from 0.2 to 0.1.

node-9.label: ECG/Holter shows first-degree AV block with bifascicular block and intermittent third-degree AV block (minimum HR 36 bpm)

node-10.label: Echocardiography shows normal EF and wall motion, left atrial enlargement, and mild pulmonary hypertension

node-11.label: High-grade atrioventricular block (bradyarrhythmia) is the underlying cause of cardiac syncope

why.why: The Radiologist analysis explicitly concludes that exertional dyspnea and syncope are best explained by cardiac syncope due to high-grade AV block, and ECG/Holter confirms first-degree AV block with bifascicular block and intermittent third-degree AV block (minimum HR 36 bpm). Echocardiography excludes severe structural disease. This direct expert corroboration of the bradyarrhythmic mechanism raises confidence from 0.9 to 0.95.
